t:
That the President is hereby authorized to bring into effect on the part of the United States the agreement between the United States of America and the United Nations regarding the headquarters of the United Nations, signed at Lake Success, New York, on June 26, 1947 (hereinafter referred to as the “agreement”), with such changes therein not contrary to the general tenor thereof and not imposing any additional obligations on the United States as the President may deem necessary and appropriate,  and at his discretion, after consultation with the appropriate State and local authorities, to enter into such supplemental agreements with the United Nations as may be necessary to fulfill the purposes of the said agreement: 
Provided, That any supplemental agreement entered into pursuant to section 5 of the agreement incorporated herein shall be submitted to the Congress for approval. The agreement follows:


    AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE UNITED NATIONS AND THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA REGARDING THE HEADQUARTERS OF THE UNITED NATIONS

Desiring to conclude an agreement for the purpose of carrying out the Resolution adopted by the General Assembly on 14 December 1946 to establish the seat of the United Nations in The City of New York and to regulate questions arising as a result thereof;
Have appointed as their representatives for this purpose:
The United Nations:

Trygve Lie,

Secretary-General,

and
The United States of America:
George C. Marshall,
Secretary of State,
Who have agreed as follows:

  

In witness whereof the respective representatives have signed this Agreement and have affixed their seals hereto.

Done in duplicate, in the English and French languages, both authentic, at Lake Success the twenty-sixth day of June 1947.
For the Government of the United States of America:

George C. Marshall
Secretary of State

For the United Nations:

Trygve Lie
Secretary-General

fable.w: The President may enter into supplemental agreements with the United Nations only after consulting the appropriate State and local authorities, who are outside the federal government. That is consultation with outside parties before a federal decision. The tempting "No" reading treats this as a past international agreement plus submission to Congress for approval, both of which stay outside the definition, but the State and local consultation clause is a forward-looking requirement that crosses the federal boundary.
fable.s: after consultation with the appropriate State and local authorities, to enter into such supplemental agreements with the United Nations as may be necessary to fulfill the purposes of the said agreement

qwen_block.w: The section explicitly requires the President to consult with 'appropriate State and local authorities' before entering into supplemental agreements. State and local authorities are outside the federal government, and this consultation occurs before a federal decision (entering the agreement) is made. This fits the definition of participation as coordination with outside entities.
qwen_block.s: after consultation with the appropriate State and local authorities, to enter into such supplemental agreements with the United Nations

opus.w: Before the President decides to enter into supplemental agreements with the UN, he must consult the appropriate state and local authorities. These are non-federal governments, so the consultation crosses the federal boundary. Sending supplemental agreements to Congress for approval stays inside the government, and the UN agreement itself is just the subject of the authorization. Neither of those makes this participation; the required state and local consultation does.
opus.s: and at his discretion, after consultation with the appropriate State and local authorities, to enter into such supplemental agreements with the United Nations as may be necessary to fulfill the purposes of the said agreement
opus.b: The tempting-but-wrong reading is that this section only covers an international agreement and sending supplemental agreements to Congress. On that reading the answer would be "No," because Congress is inside the federal government and the agreement is with the UN. That reading misses a separate clause: before the President enters into supplemental agreements, he must consult state and local authorities. Those authorities are outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section authorizes the President to enter into supplemental agreements with the United Nations only after consulting with appropriate State and local authorities. State and local authorities are outside the federal government, and this consultation occurs before the federal action of entering into the agreement, fitting the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: at his discretion, after consultation with the appropriate State and local authorities, to enter into such supplemental agreements with the United Nations as may be necessary to fulfill the purposes of the said agreement
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consultation with the appropriate State and local authorities" constitutes participation because states and local governments are outside the federal government. However, the definition requires that the consultation happen *before* making a decision. Here, the President is authorized to enter into agreements *after* consultation, but the primary action is the execution of an international treaty/agreement, and the consultation is a procedural step for the President's discretion. More importantly, the definition states: "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government **before making a decision**." While the text says "after consultation... to enter into such supplemental agreements," this is a specific authorization for the President to act. Is this "participation"? The definition includes "consultation or coordination with states, tribes, local governments... before a federal action." The text says "after consultation... to enter into... agreements". This implies the consultation happens before the entry into the agreement. So, is it participation? Yes, it involves consulting with state/local authorities (outside) before the President (federal) enters into an agreement (decision/action).

Wait, let's look closer. "at his discretion, after consultation with the appropriate State and local authorities, to enter into such supplemental agreements". This fits the definition: "consultation or coordination with states... before a federal action". The federal action is entering into the supplemental agreement. The consultation is with state/local authorities. This is "Yes".

However, let's check the "No" traps. "reports to... Congress" is No. "consultation... BETWEEN federal agencies" is No. This is consultation with State and local authorities. That is outside. So it should be Yes.

Let's double check if there's a reason to say No. Is the "decision" just the President's discretion? The definition says "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult... before making a decision." The President makes the decision to enter the agreement. He consults with state/local authorities before doing so. This fits.

Let's look at the "confidence". It's a clear case of consulting with outside entities (state/local) before a federal action (entering agreement).
